office: the Population and Immigration Authority (Misrad Hapnim)

routes.label: in person at a Population and Immigration Authority bureau, by appointment

note: Nefesh B'Nefesh's guides to Israel's government services: every Israeli is issued a Teudat Zehut on turning 16, applied for in person at a bureau (with a parent under 18); a first ID, the biometric one included, is always free. A replacement of a lost card isn't modelled. The Authority's own site (gov.il) refused this session, and the card's term and the time aren't on the guides, so they're null.

sources.title: Nefesh B'Nefesh, Biometric FAQs
sources.said: A: First ID’s are always free, same goes for a first biometric ID.

sources.title: Nefesh B'Nefesh, Teudat Zehut – Israeli Identification
sources.said: Every Israeli adult is issued a Teudat Zehut (Israeli personal identification) upon turning 16. ... A resident or citizen aged 16 years and over will be able to obtain a smart biometric ID card by personally appearing at a Population and Immigration Authority bureau
